title: Processing a Manifest

children:
During the manifesting process, the system transmits container-specific 
 information (such as its weight, carrier, and carrier service) to the Progistics 
third-party rating application. Progistics then contacts the carrier's server and manifests 
 the container. It also retrieves the container's tracking number and its 
 rate. Finally, Progistics transmits this information back to the system. The 
 system displays this information (as a "manifest") on the Manifest 
 Insight, and on the shipment line record. The Manifest Insight Screen can be used to research and perform actions on 
 manifests.
Using the Shipping Container Insight Screen
The following is discussed in this topic:

Viewing the Containers 
 on a Manifest

Removing a Container 
 from a Manifest
Viewing the Containers on a Manifest...

In the Manifest Insight, you can view the containers that make 
 up a manifest. The system will display basic container information, such 
 as tracking number and container ID, in the record list. This is especially helpful if you need to quickly reference a container ID or tracking number.

Open the Manifest 
 Insight Screen, and access the appropriate manifest.

Select the View Containers action. The Shipping Container Insight Screen will open and the system will 
 display the containers associated with the selected manifest in the record 
 list.
NOTE: You can search for manifested containers from the Shipping Container Insight Screen by turning on the "Include only manifested containers" toggle.
Removing a Container from a Manifest...

You can remove container(s) 
 from the manifest before the manifest is closed. As long as the manifest is open, 
 the customer will not be charged for the container. This is helpful if 
 a shipment has already been closed, but a container needs to come off 
 the manifest.
Access the Shipping Container Insight screen, and access the appropriate container.

Select the Remove From Manifest action. The system 
 will delete the container from the manifest.

You can close a manifests using the Manifest Insight. Note that once 
 you close a manifest, you cannot remove containers from it.

You can determine whether or not the system runs close manifest as a batch process by configuring the rating system value "Submit Close Manifest to Batch". Below are some notes about this batch process:
When a close manifest action is submitted to a batch process, the system sets the manifest to Closed. Turn the Include Closed Manifest toggle to On to view the closed manifests.
You cannot do any modifications to a manifest while it is processing.
If the system encounters an error during the close manifest process, the manifest's icon will change to red.

The system will not display to you any errors which are encountered during the batch process (they will instead be logged in process history). Note that the error messages logged in the history are retrieved from Progistics.

Access the Manifest 
 Insight Screen, and select the manifest you want to close.

Select Close form the Action menu. The system 
 will display the Close Manifest screen:

- To print a copy of the manifest, 
 make sure that the Print the Manifest toggle is ON.

- To print a UPS summary barcode 
 label, make sure that the Print Summary Barcode 
 Label toggle is ON. The system will then automatically print 
 this label after the manifest is closed.    
 Note that this check box will only appear if you are trying to close a UPS manifest.

- To transmit this manifest electronically 
 to the carrier, make sure the Transmit the Manifest toggle is ON. The system will transmit the manifest information to the carrier. 
 Note that if this carrier does not support EDI 
 transmissions, this check box will not be input capable and you will not be 
 able to select it.
Note on Ineligible Containers on the Manifest:

If there are containers on the manifest that have not yet reached a status that is considered ready to ship, then the system will enable Ineligible containers options. For most carriers (such as UPS), you will be able to choose from three options when closing the manifest: move these containers to another manifest for today (if configured for multiple manifests), move these containers to the next shipping day's manifest, or to not move these containers off the manifest. For FedEx containers or containers using a web service, the system does not support moving ineligible containers off the manifest.

Once the manifest 
 is closed, 
 it will be displayed in the Closed Summary field of the Manifest Insight Screen.
Note on Multiple Manifests Per Day

Usually, one manifest is closed per 
 day, per carrier. If you have configured to allow multiple manifests closed daily, then the 
 system will identify each manifest by assigning it a number. For example, the second manifest 
that is closed will be assigned a "#2", the third manifest that is closed will be assigned a"#3", etc.

You can print this document when you close a manifest, or you can print 
 it later. The procedures below describe how to print a manifest for a 
 closed container. Container manifests are generated in Progistics 
 CS and routed to printers through the system. You can define this document's 
 printer on the Document Routing Window. Note that the term "container 
 manifest" is a SCALE term. Carriers may refer to these documents as 
 "parcel manifests" or "summary manifests."

Access the Manifest 
 Insight, and use the treeview 
 to drill down to the manifest level of the Closed Node.

Right click on 
 the manifest you want to print the Container Manifest for and select Print. 
 Progistics 
 will generate and print the document.
